hero.title: One case file, every document.
hero.subtitle: BriefXtract is Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) built for one job: turning the day's post into a case a counselor can open and trust.

what.title: What is BriefXtract?
what.body: BriefXtract is intelligent document processing (IDP) software for debt and social counseling centres in Germany, made by Brief Insights in Berlin. A centre scans or forwards the day's post as one mixed PDF. BriefXtract splits it into documents, identifies each one — letter, court order, invoice, collection letter or notice — and extracts the creditor, file number, amount and due date. Every value is shown beside the line it was read from, so a counselor can check it against the page. Eviction notices, court deadlines and enforcement orders are flagged on arrival. Documents that belong to the same debt are linked into one case record, which can be exported in your format or passed to your case-management system through an API. Processing runs on AWS inside the EU, documents are deleted immediately afterwards, and nothing is used to train a model.

faq.title: Questions counseling centres ask.
faq.lead: Short answers, each one checkable against the rest of this site.

items.a: The post a counseling centre receives for a client: letters from creditors, collection letters, invoices, court orders and enforcement notices. Scan or forward them together as one mixed PDF; BriefXtract separates and identifies each document.

items.q: What does BriefXtract extract from a letter?
items.a: The document type, the creditor, the file number, the amount and the due date. Each value keeps a pointer to the line it was read from, and values that need a second look are marked.

items.q: How does a counselor check the results?
items.a: By reading the page, not by trusting a score. Every extracted field sits beside its source line, so confirming a case means comparing the two.

items.q: Does it work with our case-management system?
items.a: BriefXtract returns structured data in the format you need, or connects directly to your case-management system through an API, so nothing has to be retyped.

items.q: Where is client data processed, and is it kept?
items.a: On AWS infrastructure inside the EU, including the AI models on Amazon Bedrock. Documents are deleted immediately after processing and are never used to train a model.

items.q: How much time does BriefXtract save?
items.a: It is designed to bring case preparation from 1 to 8 hours per client down to about 15 minutes. That is a product target, not a measured result.

hero.title: Read, returned, deleted.
hero.subtitle: Every part of the processing path was designed with German and church data protection law in mind. It was not added afterwards.

lifecycle.title: What happens to a document.
lifecycle.lead: Four stages, and the last one is deletion. There is no fifth.

items.title: Received
items.body: The upload travels over TLS 1.3 into EU infrastructure and is held encrypted at rest with AES-256.

items.title: Processed
items.body: Classification and extraction run inside the EU. No document is used to train a model.

items.title: Returned
items.body: The structured case goes to your case-management system. The centre holds the record.

items.title: Deleted
items.body: The source document is permanently deleted immediately after processing. Nothing is stored or indexed.

commitments.title: The commitments, in writing.

items.title: Article 28 processing
items.body: A full data processing agreement (DPA) is available on request. Client data is processed in full compliance with EU GDPR.

items.title: Hosted in the EU
items.body: All processing runs on AWS infrastructure within the EU. No client document leaves the EU.

items.title: Zero data retention
items.body: Documents are permanently deleted immediately after processing. Nothing is stored, indexed or used for training.

items.title: KDG and DSG-EKD
items.body: Compliant with Catholic (KDG) and Protestant (DSG-EKD) data protection law, for Caritas, Diakonie and AWO centres.

items.title: Encrypted end to end
items.body: TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest, at every step a client's financial data passes through.

items.title: Audited infrastructure
items.body: Enterprise AI infrastructure with no model training, full auditability and a 99.9% uptime service level agreement (SLA).

faq.title: Questions a data protection officer asks.

items.a: Inside the EU, on AWS infrastructure, for the duration of processing only. The extracted case is returned to your system and the source document is deleted. Nothing is kept afterwards.

items.q: Do client documents train your models?
items.a: No. Client data never trains AI models. Documents are processed, returned as a structured case and permanently deleted.

items.q: Will you sign a data processing agreement?
items.a: Yes. A full data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 is available on request. Ask for it in your demo request.

items.q: Does this satisfy KDG and DSG-EKD?
items.a: Yes. BriefXtract is compliant with Catholic (KDG) and Protestant (DSG-EKD) data protection law, and was built for Caritas, Diakonie and AWO centres.
All processing runs on AWS infrastructure within the EU, including the AI models, which run on Amazon Bedrock.

hero.title: Built for the people who help people.
hero.subtitle: Brief Insights is a Berlin software company. It builds one product, for one end of the job: the paperwork that stands between a counselor and an appointment.

why.title: Why this exists.
why.p1: Nine per cent of Germany is in debt, and the people who help with it spend their first hours on an envelope rather than on a conversation. Thirty to eighty letters arrive per client — court orders, enforcement notices, invoices, collection letters — and every one of them is sorted, read and retyped by hand before counseling can start.
why.p2: Brief Insights was founded in Berlin to take that work off the desk. BriefXtract reads the post, extracts the fields that matter and files each document against the case, so the hour that went into sorting goes back to the person waiting for the appointment.
